2027-07-19.title: Monday of the ninth week after Pentecost · Morth Makrina
readings: The mystery of lawlessness is already at work; the Lord Jesus will destroy it; the love of the truth that saves
The Pharisees ask for a sign from heaven: “no sign will be given to this generation”
2027-07-19.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers Morth Makrina (മൊർത്ത് മക്രീന, St Macrina the Younger, died 379), the sister of St Basil the Great and St Gregory of Nyssa. Morth is the Syriac title given to a holy woman, as Mar is given to a holy man.
2027-07-19.verse: Why does this generation ask for a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.
theo: Today's Epistle is among the hardest passages in all of Paul, and it helps to remember why he wrote it. Some in Thessalonica had been shaken by a rumour that the day of the Lord had already come, and Paul writes to steady them. He speaks of “the mystery of lawlessness”: “For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work, but only until the one who now restrains it is removed. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth, annihilating him by the manifestation of his coming.” Christians have read this passage in many ways over the centuries, and the Church has never turned it into a timetable. What she takes from it is plain. Evil is real and works through deception, with “signs” and “wonders” that are false. But the Lord Jesus needs no great army to overcome it: the breath of his mouth is enough. And the reason why some are lost is not that God hides the truth but that they “refused to love the truth and so be saved.” The danger Paul names is a heart that has stopped loving what is true.

That is exactly the heart we meet in the Gospel. The Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus, “asking him for a sign from heaven, to test him.” Only a few verses earlier, Mark has told us that Jesus fed four thousand people with seven loaves, with baskets left over. The signs were there. What they wanted was not a sign but a proof on their own terms, so that they could stay in charge of the question. Mark tells us something we do not often hear about the Lord: “And he sighed deeply in his spirit and said, ‘Why does this generation ask for a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.’” It is not anger; it is the deep sigh of one who loves and is grieved by a closed door. Then he does a quiet and painful thing: “And he left them, and getting into the boat again, he went across to the other side.” The Lord does not force himself on those who test him. In the other Gospels he adds that the one sign given will be the sign of Jonah, his own death and rising. In the Holy Qurbono that sign is given to us again every Sunday.

On this day the Panchangam remembers Morth Makrina, whom the Church calls Macrina the Younger. Her brother, St Gregory of Nyssa, wrote her Life soon after she died in the year 379, and he tells us how a young woman of a Christian family in Cappadocia became the teacher of her whole family. After the death of her fiancé she chose to remain unmarried, and with her mother, Emmelia, she turned the family estate on the river Iris into a community in which women and men lived by prayer, psalm-singing and work, sharing their goods with the poor. She helped her brother Basil, who had come home proud of his learning in the schools, to turn towards a life with Christ; she raised her youngest brother, Peter, who became bishop of Sebaste; and Gregory, bishop of Nyssa, calls her his teacher. When he visited her in her last illness, he found her lying on a plank on the ground, and he heard her speak so clearly about the soul and the resurrection that he later wrote their conversation as a book. She died after a prayer of thanksgiving, signing herself with the cross.

Macrina never asked for a sign, and she never performed one that we would call a show. Her life was the sign: a quiet, steady, hidden holiness in which the whole family came to see Christ. That is what the Lord means when he refuses a sign to the testing crowd and offers himself to those who love the truth. In our own time many look for a sign in every new claim and every dramatic report of a vision, and forget the ordinary signs God has already given: the Gospel, the Holy Qurbono, the forgiveness of sins, and the faithful lives of people like Macrina. Let us ask for what she had: a heart that loves the truth and does not need to test the Lord, and a faith that shows itself in sharing the household's bread with the poor. As the monsoon rain wakes the fields each year without any announcement, so God's grace works quietly in a hidden life.
outline: Ask: do I believe because I love the truth, or do I keep asking for one more proof?
Evil is real and deceives, but the breath of the Lord's mouth is enough to overcome it.
The danger is not hidden truth but a heart that refuses to love it.
Jesus sighs and leaves; faith cannot be made to order.
A hidden life of prayer and sharing that taught a whole family.
“Why does this generation ask for a sign?”
live: Take one question of faith you have put off, and read the Gospel passage on it today, asking only what it really says.
This week, do not ask God for proof before you do what you already know is right. Do it first, and trust.
Do one hidden good deed at home this week, as Macrina did, without comment: a shared meal, a lamp lit, a visit paid.
2027-07-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you sighed in your spirit over those who asked for a sign, and you give yourself to those who love the truth. Keep us from the deception of false wonders, and guard us from the evil one. Give us a heart that loves what is true and does not set conditions for you. Through the prayers of Morth Makrina, who taught her whole family by a hidden life of prayer, psalms and charity, make our homes places where your light is seen, and make us ready for the day of your coming. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The sign the Lord has given us is the sign of Jonah: his death and rising, which we proclaim at every Holy Qurbono; and there, without any show, the bread and wine become his Body and Blood for those who love the truth.
conn: 2 Thessalonians 2:10: “because they refused to love the truth and so be saved”; Psalm 25:5: “Lead me in your truth, and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation.”
Matthew 12:39: “An evil and adulterous generation asks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.”
Psalm 95:8–9: “do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness, when your ancestors tested me”; Hebrews 3:15 repeats the warning.
fathers: Writing of his sister Macrina, he says that for their youngest brother Peter she was father, teacher, guardian, mother and counsellor in every good (Life of Macrina, in substance).
In the dialogue he wrote after her death, Macrina teaches that the resurrection is the restoration of human nature to what it was in the beginning (On the Soul and the Resurrection, in substance).
magis: Jesus accompanies his words with mighty works, wonders and signs, which show that the kingdom is present in him; but these signs do not remove the need for faith, and they are not given to those who ask for them out of curiosity or the desire for magic (in substance).

Before Christ's second coming the Church must pass through a final trial that will shake the faith of many believers; the deception of evil is an imposture that offers a solution to human problems at the price of apostasy from the truth (in substance).
All the faithful of whatever rank or state are called to the fullness of Christian life and to the perfection of charity (in substance).

quick: Paul warns that the mystery of lawlessness is at work, but the Lord Jesus will destroy it with the breath of his mouth; the lost are those who refused to love the truth.
The Pharisees ask for a sign from heaven to test Jesus; he sighs, refuses, and crosses to the other side.
The Panchangam remembers Morth Makrina, sister of Basil and Gregory of Nyssa, whose hidden holy life taught her whole family.
2027-07-19.action: Do not ask God for a sign today. Do the thing you already know is right, quietly.
2027-07-19.question: Do I believe because I love the truth, or because I keep asking for more proof?

family.explain: Some people asked Jesus to show them a special sign, but they were not really listening. Jesus felt sad, and he went away. God has already given us many signs of his love: the Gospel, the Holy Qurbono, the beauty of the world, and good people. Today we remember Morth Makrina, who did nothing loud or showy. She prayed, taught her brothers, and shared with the poor, and her whole family learned about Jesus from her.
family.intention: We pray for those who have doubts about their faith, and for the grace of a quiet and honest heart.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one quiet good thing I can do today so that someone sees Jesus in it?”

illus: A young engineering student from a village near Pala came home for the holidays full of questions. At the dinner table he told his grandmother that he would believe in God when he was shown some clear proof. She did not argue. That evening, as always, she lit the lamp in the prayer corner and sat down to say her prayers with the rosary, while the monsoon rain beat on the roof. The next morning, during the heavy rain, she crossed the muddy lane with a covered dish and a warm shawl for a neighbour who was ill and alone, as she had done every day for years. The student walked behind her with an umbrella. On the way back he said, without any smile, that he had a new question: what was it that made her do this every day? She said she had never needed a sign, because she had been given a Saviour. He thought about her answer for a long time afterwards.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you gave us the sign of Jonah, your death and resurrection. Give us a heart that loves the truth and does not need to test you. Amen.
share: The mystery of lawlessness is already at work (2 Thessalonians 2:7). Where do I see deception around me?
They refused to love the truth and so be saved (2 Thessalonians 2:10). Is there a truth I am avoiding?
Why does this generation ask for a sign? (Mark 8:12). What signs has the Lord already given me?
pm.resp: Lord, give us a heart that loves the truth.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the apostolic faith and not be led astray by false signs.
For those who struggle with doubt, that they may find a patient friend and the light of the Gospel.
For families, that like Macrina's home they may be schools of prayer and charity.
For monks, nuns and all who live a hidden life of prayer.
For the poor and the sick in this rainy season, that they may be sheltered and cared for.

term: A Syriac title of honour, meaning lady, given to holy women of the Syriac tradition, as Mar (lord) is given to holy men. Morth Makrina is St Macrina the Younger.
kidsaint: The big sister who taught everyone

Macrina was the oldest in a big family. She loved Jesus very much, and she taught her little brothers to pray and to read the Psalms. One of them, Basil, became a great bishop, and another, Gregory, wrote many books. When Macrina grew up, she started a quiet home where people prayed and shared what they had with the poor. She never did anything showy, but everyone who knew her learned to love God. Lesson: you do not need a big sign to show Jesus; a quiet and kind life is a sign too.

homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel the Pharisees ask Jesus for a sign from heaven, to test him. And Mark tells us that Jesus sighed deeply in his spirit and said: Why does this generation ask for a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation (Mark 8:12). Then he left them. He had fed four thousand people with seven loaves only a few verses before. The signs were there. The problem was not a lack of signs but a lack of love for the truth.

That is also the warning in the Epistle. Paul says that the mystery of lawlessness is already at work, with false signs and wonders and deceptions for those who are perishing, because they refused to love the truth and so be saved (2 Thessalonians 2:10). He does not tell us to fear. The Lord Jesus will destroy the lawless one with the breath of his mouth (2 Thessalonians 2:8). What the Lord wants from us is a heart that loves what is true.

Today the Church remembers Morth Makrina, the sister of St Basil and St Gregory of Nyssa. Gregory wrote her Life, and he calls her his teacher. She turned her family's home into a place of prayer, psalms and charity, and she never asked for a sign. Her whole life was a sign. Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven (Matthew 5:16).
Let us ask the Lord for a heart like hers: honest, quiet and faithful. And let us not look for wonders when the Lord has already given us the Gospel and the Holy Qurbono. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine your friend says, I will only believe you love me if you do something amazing. That would make you sad, wouldn't it? That is how Jesus felt when some people asked him for a special sign. He had already done so many good things! Today we remember Morth Makrina. She showed Jesus to her brothers just by praying, teaching and sharing. You can also show Jesus to your family, just by being kind and honest every day.

The Lord Jesus overcomes without an army.

The only sign: the sign of Jonah.

concl: The Lord gives himself to those who love the truth, and gives no show to those who only test.
A quiet life of prayer and charity, like Macrina's, is a sign that God is near.
2027-07-19.resolve: Love the truth, stop testing the Lord, and shine quietly in good works.
